## The question

[Fit a table into a beamer's frame](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/395885/fit-a-table-into-a-beamers-frame), asked by user134500 on TeX Stack Exchange (2017-10-12; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> As you can see below, the **output** is too large:
>

>
>  Any idea how to diminish table's height?
>
>
>   [q-1]: https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/97505/shrink-table-to-fit-on-a-page-or-keep-it-as-it-is
>   [q-2]: https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/77998/fitting-tables-into-beamer

You've got a pretty table, but it's laid out for a portrait-oriented stock (paper) and you're trying to fit it onto landscape-oriented stock (a 16x9 slide). I suggest reorganizing to conserve vertical space.

1. You have two table captions: one of them refers to acids and alcohols, and one just to acids. There are only acids on this slide; presumably the landscape table combined them and the intent is to put them on separate slides here. Yet you have a full line for marking all of these solutions as acids. Edit all of this down to a single line and make it the slide title.
3. You have a full line grouping the RM1 results. If you combine that into the column headers, you save a line at the expense of horizontal space, of which you have plenty.
4. The `\toprule` seems unnecessary because the frame title is a horizontal rule of its own.
1. The `table` environment creates a float, and you don't want this `tabular` to float. Just delete it.

For example:

```latex
\begin{frame}{Estimación de p$K_\text{a}$ para ácidos}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{lccccc}
 &  & \multicolumn{2}{c}{RM1-COSMO} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{RM1-SS-COSMO} \\  \cmidrule(lr){3-4}\cmidrule(lr){5-6}
 & p$K\text{a}_{\text{exp}}$\SI{298}{K} & p$K\text{a}_{\text{calc}}$ & $\Delta$p$K\text{a}$ & p$K\text{a}_{\text{calc}}$ & $\Delta$p$K\text{a}$ \\  \midrule
Ácido acético & 4.75 & 2.1 & 2.6 & 4.2 & 0.6 \\  
fluoroacético & 2.59 & -0.8 & 3.3 & -0.8 & 3.4 \\  
fórmico & 3.75 & ref & - & ref & - \\  
pirúvico & 2.39 & -3.0 & 5.4 & 0.7 & 1.7 \\  
glioxílico & 3.18 & -2.3 & 5.5 & 0.4 & 2.8 \\  
propanoico & 4.86 & 2.3 & 2.5 & 3.9 & 0.9 \\  
butanoico & 4.83 & 2.6 & 2.3 & 4.2 & 0.7 \\  
acrílico & 4.25 & 2.0 & 2.3 & 1.0 & 3.3 \\  
láctico & 3.86 & 0.7 & 3.2 & 5.0 & -1.2 \\  
benzoico & 4.2 & 1.1 & 3.1 & 1.6 & 2.6 \\  
MAE &  &  & 3.1 &  & 1.8 \\  \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{frame}
```
